A lack of sleep makes it hard to pay attention in class, and it can also change a person's mood. To sleep better, experts suggest a few simple habits. First, go to bed at the same time every night. Second, keep your room dark and quiet. Finally, turn off your phone an hour before bed. These small changes help many young people feel better the next day.

He did not like cakes or sweet food.
He is shy and has poor hearing.
He had just moved into the building.

questions.explanation: for 뒤에는 기간이 와요. Monday, last week, yesterday는 시점이라 since와 함께 써요.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does 'had' help form the past perfect?

questions.explanation: 첫 문장의 had는 finished와 함께 과거완료를 이루는 조동사예요. 나머지의 had는 '먹었다', '해야 했다'는 뜻의 본동사예요.

questions.prompt: In which sentence does 'have' help form the present perfect?

questions.explanation: had eaten은 전화가 온 과거 시점보다 먼저 끝난 일을 나타내요.

questions.explanation: 현재완료는 과거의 일이 지금까지 영향을 줄 때 써요. 나머지는 과거에 이미 끝난 일이에요.

questions.explanation: Have you ever + p.p.?는 지금까지의 경험을 묻는 표현이에요.

questions.prompt: Choose the best answer: "I ___ you for ages! Where have you been?"

questions.explanation: 오랫동안 못 본 것이 지금까지 이어지므로 현재완료 부정 haven't seen을 써요.

questions.prompt: Choose the best answer: "Sam ___ his speech by the time the guests arrive tonight."

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: 부정 분사구문은 Not + -ing로 써요. 분사구문 안에 do동사는 쓰지 않아요.

questions.prompt: “Since the road had been closed by snow, the bus took another route.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?

options.text: The road been closed by snow, the bus took another route.
Having been closed by snow, the bus took another route.
The road having been closed by snow, the bus took another route.
The road having closed by snow, the bus took another route.

questions.explanation: 종속절 주어(the road)가 주절 주어(the bus)와 다르므로 주어를 남기고, 완료 수동은 having been + 과거분사로 써요.

questions.prompt: “If you turn right at the bank, you'll find the post office.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?

options.text: Turning right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
Turns right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
To turn right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
Turned right at the bank, you'll find the post office.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 주어(you)가 직접 방향을 ‘도는’ 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 Turning을 써요.

questions.prompt: “While she was waiting for the bus, Eve read a book.”을 접속사를 남기고 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?

options.text: While waiting for the bus, Eve read a book.
While to wait for the bus, Eve read a book.
While waited for the bus, Eve read a book.
While wait for the bus, Eve read a book.

questions.explanation: ‘주어 + be동사’를 생략하고 접속사 While 뒤에 -ing를 남겨요.

questions.prompt: “Walking along the beach, Sora found a shell.”과 같은 뜻의 문장은?

options.text: While Sora walks along the beach, she found a shell.

While Sora was walking along the beach, she found a shell.
Because Sora found a shell, she walked along the beach.

questions.explanation: 분사구문의 시제는 주절을 따라 과거예요. 해변을 걷는 동안 조개를 발견했다는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: “Not wanting to disturb her, I left quietly.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

When I wanted to disturb her, I left quietly.

questions.explanation: Not + -ing 분사구문은 여기서 ‘~하고 싶지 않아서’라는 이유를 나타내요.

questions.prompt: “Seen from the sky, the island looks like a heart.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

options.text: Although it is seen from the sky, the island looks like a heart.

When it sees the sky, the island looks like a heart.

questions.explanation: Seen은 수동 의미이므로 절로 바꾸면 it is seen이 돼요.

questions.prompt: “Having missed the last train, they took a taxi.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

Because they missed the last train, they will take a taxi.
After they took a taxi, they had missed the last train.

questions.explanation: 완료 분사구문은 주절보다 앞선 일을 나타내므로 절에서는 had missed가 돼요.

questions.prompt: “Weather permitting, the match will be held on Sunday.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

If the weather permitted, the match will be held on Sunday.

questions.explanation: Weather permitting은 ‘날씨가 허락하면’이라는 조건이에요. unless는 반대 뜻이 돼요.

questions.prompt: “The meeting being over, everyone went home.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

Before the meeting was over, everyone went home.

questions.explanation: 독립분사구문 The meeting being over는 ‘회의가 끝난 뒤(끝났으므로)’의 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: “Having no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

options.text: If he has no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
Although he had no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
After he talked to everyone, Daeho felt lonely.
Since he had no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Having no one ~은 이유를 나타내므로 Since/Because를 써서 바꿔요.

questions.prompt: “Being a doctor, she knows how to treat a fever.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: ‘의사이기 때문에’ 열을 치료할 줄 안다는 뜻이므로 이유예요.

questions.prompt: “The train left at six, arriving in Daegu at nine.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 문장 뒤에 오는 -ing는 ‘그리고 ~했다’처럼 이어지는 결과나 연속 동작을 나타내요.

questions.prompt: “Reaching the top of the hill, we sat down to rest.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: ‘언덕 꼭대기에 닿았을 때’라는 뜻의 시간이에요.

questions.prompt: “Left in direct sunlight, chocolate melts quickly.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘햇빛에 그대로 두면’이라는 뜻이므로 조건이에요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 분사구문이 양보(~이지만)의 뜻을 나타내는 문장은?

options.text: Opening the box, Tom began to smile.
Turning off the light, you can save energy.
Feeling dizzy, Rina sat down at once.
Living near the sea, Dan can't swim.

questions.explanation: 바다 근처에 살지만 수영을 못한다는 뜻이라 양보예요. 나머지는 각각 이유, 시간, 조건에 가까워요.

questions.prompt: “Driving to work, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?

questions.explanation: Driving의 의미상 주어는 사람이어야 해요. 엔진이나 소리는 운전할 수 없으므로 나머지는 틀려요.

questions.prompt: “Climbing the mountain, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?

questions.explanation: ‘올라가는’ 주체가 주절의 주어여야 해요. 보기 중 hikers만 산을 오를 수 있어요.

questions.prompt: “Having eaten too much, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?

questions.explanation: 먹은 사람이 주절의 주어여야 해요. 피자, 복통, 배는 ‘먹은’ 주체가 될 수 없어요.

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 어색한 문장은?

questions.prompt: “Running for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.”를 바르게 고친 문장은?

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 주어가 주절의 주어와 달라도 맞는 문장은?

questions.explanation: 종속절과 주절의 주어가 다르면(Hana / everyone) 주어를 남겨서 독립분사구문으로 써야 해요.

questions.explanation: 보고서는 ‘쓰인’ 수동 관계이므로 Written이에요.

questions.explanation: 편지는 ‘보내진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 sent예요.

questions.explanation: 아이들이 놀람을 ‘느끼는’ 쪽이므로 과거분사 amazed예요.

questions.prompt: “그 소년은 편지를 읽는 동안 울었다.”(동시 동작)를 나타내는 문장은?

questions.prompt: “Because Tom had not studied, he failed the test.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?

options.text: Not to have studied, Tom failed the test.
Not having study, Tom failed the test.
Not having studied, Tom failed the test.
Not studied, Tom failed the test.

questions.explanation: 먼저 일어난 일의 부정은 Not having + 과거분사로 써요.

questions.prompt: “Having bought the tickets, Jenny went to the cinema.”에서 일어난 순서는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: 완료 분사구문(Having + 과거분사)은 주절보다 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내요.

questions.prompt: “Generally speaking, summers in Korea are hot and humid.”에서 Generally speaking과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 표현은?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Generally speaking은 ‘일반적으로’라는 뜻으로 In general과 같아요.

questions.prompt: “Judging from his accent, he must be from the south.”에서 Judging from의 뜻은?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Judging from ~은 ‘~로 판단하면’이라는 뜻의 관용 표현이에요.

questions.prompt: “Considering her age, she plays the violin very well.”에서 Considering의 뜻은?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Considering ~은 ‘~을 고려하면, ~치고는’이라는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 부정형이 틀린 문장은?

options.text: Not having been told, Jay arrived late.
Not wanting to wake the baby, she whispered.
Don't knowing the way, we asked a stranger.
Never having seen snow, the boy ran outside.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 분사구문에서는 do동사를 쓰지 않고 Not + -ing로 써요.

questions.prompt: 완료 분사구문이 틀린 문장은?

options.text: Having been praised by the coach, Lee smiled.
Having cooked dinner, Mom called us to the table.
Having overslept, Tim missed the first bus.
Having ate lunch, Sam went back to work.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Having 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 해요. ate가 아니라 eaten이에요.

questions.prompt: with + 목적어 + 분사 구문이 틀린 문장은?

options.text: Tom sat with his arms folded.
The cat sat by the door with its ears pointing up.
Mia walked with her hair blowing in the wind.
My brother stood at the door with his shoes taking off.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: 신발은 ‘벗겨진’ 수동 관계이므로 with his shoes off 또는 taken off가 맞아요.

questions.prompt: 수동 의미의 분사구문이 올바르게 쓰인 문장은?

options.text: Written by a famous poet, I enjoyed this poem very much.

Written by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.
Writes by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘쓰인’ 것은 시이므로 주절의 주어도 this poem이어야 해요. 첫 번째 보기는 주어가 I라서 틀려요.

questions.prompt: “창밖을 바라보며 그는 한숨을 쉬었다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

Looked out the window, he sighed.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 동시 동작은 -ing 분사구문으로 나타내요. 주어(he)와 분사의 의미상 주어가 일치해야 해요.

questions.prompt: “그녀는 음악을 들으며 숙제를 했다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: She did her homework listening to music.
She did her homework to listening to music.
She did her homework listen to music.
She did her homework listened to music.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 문장 뒤에 -ing를 붙이면 ‘~하면서’라는 동시 동작을 나타낼 수 있어요.

questions.prompt: “그는 방을 나가면서 뒤로 문을 닫았다.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: He left the room, closing the door behind him.
He left the room, to closing the door behind him.
He left the room, closes the door behind him.
He left the room, closed the door behind him.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 연속 동작은 문장 뒤에 -ing 분사구문으로 이어 붙여요.

questions.prompt: 두 문장의 뜻이 서로 다른 것은?

options.text: Not knowing the way, I asked a police officer. = As I did not know the way, I asked a police officer.
Having eaten dinner, I washed the dishes. = I washed the dishes before I ate dinner.
Walking home, Joon saw a rainbow. = While Joon was walking home, he saw a rainbow.
Seen from afar, the tower looks small. = When it is seen from afar, the tower looks small.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Having eaten은 ‘먹은 뒤에’라는 뜻이므로 먹기 전에 설거지했다는 풀이는 틀려요.

questions.prompt:
Standing on the rocky shore at low tide, you can find a tiny world hidden in the pools left by the sea. Protected from the waves, small crabs and sea stars live there quietly. Their lives are not easy, however. Heated by the sun, the shallow water can become much warmer than the open sea, and the animals must cope with the sudden change. When the tide returns, fresh cold water rushes in, bringing food and cooling everything down. Having survived such changes every day, tide pool animals have become very tough. Scientists study them, hoping to learn how living things may react to a warmer planet.

What is the passage mainly about?

Why scientists prefer the sea to rocky shores for their research
How tide pool animals deal with daily change
How the open sea becomes warmer than the land every summer

questions.prompt:
Many teenagers keep their phones beside the bed, scrolling through videos until late at night. Though entertaining, this habit can damage sleep. The bright screen sends a signal to the brain that it is still daytime, delaying the release of the hormone that makes us sleepy. questions.prompt:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all sea life. Built slowly by tiny animals called corals, a reef can take thousands of years to form. The corals live together with algae, which give them food and bright colors. When the water becomes too warm, stressed corals push out the algae and turn white, a process called bleaching. Bleached reefs are not dead, but they are weak. Given enough time and cooler water, they can recover. Unfortunately, warming seas, polluted rivers, and careless tourists, touching or breaking the coral, make recovery difficult in many places. Protecting reefs therefore requires action at local and global levels.

Why coral reefs matter and what puts them at risk

questions.prompt:
Walking across a stone bridge built five hundred years ago, you may wonder why it is still standing. The answer lies in its shape. Unlike a flat beam, an arch pushes the weight outward and downward, spreading the load along curved stones. Pressed tightly together, the stones lock in place, and the heavier the load, the tighter they hold. Builders of the past, working without modern math, learned these lessons by trial and error. Failed bridges taught them what worked. Today, engineers still copy the arch, though they build it with steel and concrete. Having proved its strength for centuries, the arch remains one of the safest shapes in construction.

What is the main point of the passage?

options.text: Flat beams are the safest shape for long bridges.
The arch shape explains why old bridges stay strong.
Past builders used math to make perfect bridges.
Modern engineers have stopped using stone for bridges.

Students gave a morning to help a shelter.
A shelter asked for more dogs to be adopted.

questions.prompt:
My violin teacher once told me, "Whatever you play, play it slowly first." I did not understand until my last recital. For weeks I had rushed through the hard passages, hoping speed would hide my mistakes. Whenever I performed in front of my family, the same notes went wrong. Then I followed her advice and practised each bar at half speed, however boring it felt. Slowly, my fingers learned the shape of the music. At the recital, my hands were shaking, but they remembered what to do. I did not play perfectly, whereas the girl before me did. Still, I walked off the stage smiling, because I knew exactly why each note sounded the way it did.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: A recital is easier than practice at home.
The teacher stopped the writer's lessons.
Slow practice made the writer play better.
Playing quickly is the secret of good music.

questions.prompt:
Many teenagers struggle to wake up early, and parents often blame laziness. However, scientists point to biology instead. During adolescence, the body begins to release the sleep hormone melatonin later at night, so young people feel awake long after adults feel tired. As a result, a student who goes to bed at midnight may get only six hours of sleep before a seven o'clock class. Some schools have therefore moved their start times back by an hour. Parents should punish teenagers who keep refusing to get up early.

questions.prompt:
Bread dough rises because of tiny living things called yeast. When yeast is mixed with flour and water, it feeds on the sugars in the flour. This feeding produces carbon dioxide, a gas that forms thousands of small bubbles inside the dough. The dough is stretchy, so it expands around the bubbles instead of letting them escape. If the baker kneads the dough well, the structure becomes strong enough to hold the gas. Then, when the dough is put in a hot oven, the bubbles grow even bigger before the heat finally stops the yeast and fixes the shape of the loaf. That is why a good loaf is light and full of holes.

options.text: Water turning into steam before baking
The baker pressing air in with both hands
Flour reacting with the salt in the recipe
Yeast producing gas as it feeds on sugar

questions.prompt:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they shelter about a quarter of all sea creatures. Corals get their color and much of their food from tiny algae living inside them. When the water becomes too warm, the corals push the algae out, and they turn white. This is called bleaching. questions.prompt:
Traditional Korean houses were heated by ondol, a system that warms the floor instead of the air. Smoke and hot air from a fireplace in the kitchen traveled through channels under stone slabs, and the stones kept the heat for hours. In summer, however, the same houses stayed cool because the main hall had a wooden floor that let breezes pass underneath. questions.prompt:
Deep inside a mountain in the far north, there is a vault that holds duplicates of seeds from crops around the world. Its purpose is not to grow anything today but to protect the future. If a disease or a disaster destroyed a variety of wheat in one country, scientists could ask for a sample from the vault and begin again. The storage rooms are kept cold, and the rock around them provides natural protection against heat and earthquakes. Because the seeds are only copies, each country continues to own its own samples. Critics sometimes say that the vault is an expensive precaution, but supporters answer that insurance always looks costly until the day it is needed.

A precaution may seem costly until a crisis occurs.

questions.prompt:
Offshore wind farms are rising in many coastal waters, and the reasons are easy to understand. Winds over the sea are stronger and steadier than those on land, so each turbine produces more electricity. In addition, there are few buildings to block the view, which reduces complaints from residents. On the other hand, building at sea is expensive: the towers need strong foundations, and workers must travel by boat for repairs. Fishermen also worry that the structures will take up good fishing grounds. Engineers respond that the foundations can become homes for shellfish and small fish, and some wind farms already permit fishing between the towers. Whether the benefits outweigh the costs will depend on careful planning for each location.

Why do offshore turbines produce more electricity?

options.text: Fishermen help to keep them running.
The towers at sea are always taller.
The winds at sea are stronger and steadier.
There is more sunshine over the water.

questions.prompt:
Mr. Park: Today's topic is whether schools should assign less homework. Eunji, would you start?
Eunji: Yes. I believe homework should be reduced, because many students sleep only five or six hours. Fatigue makes it harder to learn.
Taemin: I disagree. Homework gives students a chance to practice what they learned, so it helps them remember.
Eunji: Practice is important, but quality matters more than quantity. Thirty carefully chosen questions are better than a hundred repetitive ones.
Taemin: I accept that point. Nevertheless, without any homework, some students would not review at all.
Mr. Park: So is there a middle path?
Eunji: Perhaps short assignments that are checked and discussed in class.
Taemin: Then I could agree, as long as the tasks are meaningful.
Mr. Park: Thank you both. You have shown that a disagreement can lead to a better idea.

What reason does Eunji give for reducing homework?

options.text: Homework is too easy for students.
Teachers do not read the answers.

The building's residents' committee, however, listened to every worry, invited an experienced beekeeper to answer questions, and agreed to a six-month trial. The bees flew toward the city's parks, not toward the balconies, and the only visible change was a row of flowerpots that tenants planted to feed them. Animals living in these pools must survive hot sunshine, sudden rain, and waves that crash against them without warning. To invite Soyeon to another party
To blame Soyeon for a misunderstanding
To announce the end of a friendship

On the final Friday, the old town library opened its doors for the last time. Sunlight lay in long yellow stripes across the reading tables, and the smell of paper and dust seemed stronger than ever. Mr. Han, the librarian for thirty-one years, moved slowly between the shelves, straightening books that were already straight. A few old regulars sat in their usual seats, not reading, just sitting. When the clock struck five, no one stood up. The new building would be larger and brighter, but everyone knew it would be different.

An elderly man walking his dog stopped to thank us, saying he had waited years to see the river clean. I felt a surge of pride that I could not quite explain. As we sat on the grass sharing sandwiches, one volunteer said, "Imagine what we could do every month." Nobody laughed, because everyone was already imagining it.

What is the overall mood at the end of the passage?

Checking phones between cups of tea

Paper seems like a simple material, but making it from fresh trees uses a great deal of water and energy. options.text: Ink cannot be removed from the pulp.
Recyclers run out of clean water.
Its fibers become shorter each time.
Staples stay inside the new sheets.

questions.prompt:
On a summer afternoon, a paved street can be ten degrees hotter than a nearby park. Concrete and dark roads soak up sunlight all day and release it slowly after sunset, so neighborhoods with few trees stay warm even at night. Trees work in the opposite way. Their leaves block direct sunlight, and the water that evaporates from them cools the surrounding air. Several cities have therefore begun planting trees along the hottest streets first, rather than spreading them evenly. Early results are encouraging: residents say that walking outdoors feels easier, and some buildings use less electricity for air conditioning. Planting takes years to show its full effect, however, because young trees give little shade. Planners say the goal is not decoration but protecting people, especially older adults, from dangerous heat.

Choose the pair that best fills in (A) and (B).

Summary: Hard surfaces (A) heat in cities, whereas trees (B) the air, so planting them on the hottest streets can protect residents.

questions.prompt:
Many students believe that staying up all night before an exam is the best way to learn more. Sleep researchers disagree. During deep sleep, the brain replays what a person studied during the day and moves important information into long-term memory. Apps are designed to offer a steady stream of small rewards, such as a new photo or a friendly comment, and the brain learns to check for them again and again. Over time, people may find it harder to stay with a long book or a single task. Yet researchers warn against simple conclusions. Some users learn quickly from short videos, and online groups help shy people find friends who share their interests. The difference seems to lie in how the apps are used rather than whether they are used. People who set limits and choose carefully tend to feel in control, while those who scroll without a purpose report feeling tired and distracted.

What does the writer imply by saying 'researchers warn against simple conclusions'?

options.text: The effects of social media cannot be described as only good or bad.
Researchers have not studied social media for very long.
Most people already know exactly how apps change the brain.
Social media apps should be banned until more is known.

questions.prompt:
Bees are best known for honey, but their larger job is pollination. When a bee moves from flower to flower, it carries pollen that allows plants to produce fruit and seeds. A large share of the crops people eat, including apples, almonds and many vegetables, depends at least partly on this work. In recent years, beekeepers in several regions have reported that more colonies than usual are dying each winter. Scientists point to a mix of causes, such as disease, certain farm chemicals and the loss of wild flowers. No single cause explains everything, which makes the problem harder to solve. Farmers who leave strips of wild flowers beside their fields have seen healthier bees nearby. Such small changes suggest that protecting bees is possible if many people take part.

Choose the pair that best fills in (A) and (B).

Summary: Bees are (A) for food crops, yet their numbers are falling for (B) reasons, so protecting them requires many people to act.

questions.prompt:

Choose the pair that best fills in (A) and (B).

Summary: Minimalism may reduce (A) by limiting choices, but it can become (B) if it is practiced mainly for appearance.

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt:
When a forecast says there is a thirty percent chance of rain, many people think the forecast is wrong if the day stays dry. In fact, the statement describes probability, not a promise. It means that in similar conditions in the past, rain fell on about three out of ten occasions. Forecasters rely on computer models that simulate the atmosphere, but small differences in starting data can lead to different results, especially several days ahead. A single prediction can therefore never be perfectly certain. Understanding this helps us use forecasts wisely: a high chance of rain suggests carrying an umbrella, while a low chance suggests that we can take the risk. A forecast is not a verdict; it is a guide for making decisions with incomplete information.

What is the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Umbrellas are unnecessary on dry days.
Forecasters are often careless with the data they collect each day.
It rains on three days out of every ten.
Forecasts should be read as probabilities, not guarantees.

Daniel: I understand. I'll cut it to three sentences and send it again tonight.

It did not mention the title of the chapter.
It was written in a language other than English.
It had too few details about the many fish species in a reef.

Host: Dr. Lee, many people believe that dolphins never sleep. Is that true?
Dr. Lee: Not exactly. Dolphins do rest, but they do it in an unusual way.
Host: How is it different from our sleep?
Dr. Lee: A dolphin must come to the surface to breathe, so it cannot fall completely unconscious. Instead, it rests one half of its brain at a time.
Host: So the other half stays awake?
Dr. Lee: Yes. That half controls breathing and keeps an eye on the surroundings. After a few hours, the halves switch roles.
Host: That sounds very practical. Do other animals do this?
Dr. Lee: Some birds appear to rest half of their brains while flying long distances, but dolphins are the best-known example.
Host: So the idea that dolphins never sleep is a myth.
Dr. Lee: It is a simplification. They do sleep, just not in the way humans do.

What is the main point of Dr. Lee's explanation?

options.text: Dolphins breathe underwater without coming up.
Dolphins never need any rest at all.
Dolphins sleep with half the brain resting at a time.

questions.prompt:
Good communication is not only about speaking well; it also depends on how well we listen. Researchers on conversation often describe "active listening," which means giving full attention to the speaker instead of preparing your own reply. Active listeners show that they care in small ways: they look at the speaker, nod occasionally, and avoid checking their phones. They may also say "I see" or "That sounds difficult" to show that they follow the speaker's feelings. When necessary, they summarize what they heard, for example, "So you're worried about the exam on Monday?" This gives the speaker a chance to correct any misunderstanding. Surprisingly, people who feel truly heard are more likely to trust the listener and to calm down when they are upset.

What does "active listening" mean in the passage?

options.text: Taking written notes about everything a person says
Repeating every sentence in a louder voice
Paying full attention to the speaker rather than planning your answer
Speaking continuously so that the other person stays quiet and listens to you

The sweater she had bought did not fit her uncle.

In school projects, disagreement is almost unavoidable, but it does not have to lead to an argument. The key is to separate the idea from the person. Instead of saying, "That's a terrible plan," try, "I see what you mean, but I'm worried about the cost." Beginning with a point of agreement shows that you have listened. You can then use a softener such as "I'm not sure that..." or "Maybe we could..." to offer your alternative gently. It also helps to ask questions: "What do you think would happen if we changed the date?" This invites the other person to think with you rather than defend himself. If the discussion becomes heated, it is wise to take a short break. Often the best solution is a mixture of both ideas.

Work in different rooms from your partner
Criticize the plan, not the one who suggested it
Let one person make every decision

questions.prompt:
In many English-speaking countries, the usual reply to a compliment is a simple "Thank you." If someone says, "You gave a great presentation," answering "No, it was terrible" may make the speaker feel embarrassed, because it seems to reject their opinion. A better response is, "Thanks, I'm glad you enjoyed it." You may add a short comment, such as "I worked on it all weekend," to continue the conversation. Learners from cultures where modesty is valued sometimes feel it is boastful to accept praise so directly, but a warm thanks is generally considered both polite and humble. It is also friendly to return the compliment when it is sincere, for example, "Your slides looked great too." Remember that these are habits, not strict rules, and customs can differ among families and regions.

What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.text: To list the customs of one country
To explain a common way to respond to praise in English
To teach how to give a good presentation in English class
To argue that modesty is a bad habit

questions.prompt:
In many English-speaking countries, the usual reply to a compliment is a simple "Thank you." If someone says, "You gave a great presentation," answering "No, it was terrible" may make the speaker feel embarrassed, because it seems to reject their opinion. A better response is, "Thanks, I'm glad you enjoyed it." You may add a short comment, such as "I worked on it all weekend," to continue the conversation. Learners from cultures where modesty is valued sometimes feel it is boastful to accept praise so directly, but a warm thanks is generally considered both polite and humble. It is also friendly to return the compliment when it is sincere, for example, "Your slides looked great too." Remember that these are habits, not strict rules, and customs can differ among families and regions.

What is the purpose of the last sentence?

To announce that customs are all the same in English-speaking countries
To advertise a book about manners
To warn readers not to treat the advice as a fixed rule

"She has to answer honestly."

The leader organized the discussion with clear steps.
It was held outside the school.

When you work outside the office, you are still handling information that belongs to your employer and its customers. Experts therefore recommend a few simple habits. Use a strong password that is different for every account, and never share it, even with a colleague you trust. Avoid public Wi-Fi when you open private files, because other users on the same network may be able to see your activity. Lock your screen whenever you leave your desk, even at home, and do not discuss confidential matters where visitors can overhear you. In others, the host may expect guests to arrive a little late, and starting exactly on time can feel rushed. Exchanging business cards is also treated differently. In several Asian countries, people offer and receive a card with both hands and read it carefully before putting it away. Writing on it or pushing it into a back pocket may seem impolite.

First, place the speaker on a flat surface near a power outlet and plug it in. A blue light will appear and turn white after about thirty seconds. Next, download the Aria app on your phone and create an account. Once you have signed in, tap “Add device” and choose your speaker from the list. questions.prompt:
Welcome to your first week at Harbor Hotel. Guests form their first impression at the front desk, so your behaviour matters a great deal.

Always greet guests with a smile within ten seconds of their arrival, even if you are on the phone. Use their family name when you have it. When a guest has a complaint, listen without interrupting, apologize for the inconvenience, and say clearly what you will do about it. Never promise something you cannot deliver; if you are unsure, say that you will check with your manager and give a time when you will reply.

Remember, too, that guest information is private. Do not say a guest's room number aloud in the lobby. Write it down and hand it over instead.

Who is the guide written for?

Guests who stay at the hotel

Hello team,

While testing version 2.4 on my laptop this morning, I found a problem with the Save button. When I enter a note longer than 500 characters and press Save, the app freezes for about ten seconds and then closes without saving anything.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a new note.
2. Paste in a text of more than 500 characters.
3. Press Save.

Expected result: The note is saved and a confirmation message appears.
Actual result: The app freezes and closes, and the note is lost.

I tried this three times with the same result. Shorter notes work normally. Since users could lose important work, I suggest that we fix this before the release on Friday. I have attached a screen recording.

Thanks,
Ha-neul

questions.prompt:
Conference calls save time and travel costs, but they can easily go wrong without good manners. First, join a few minutes early and test your microphone so that the meeting can start on time. Keep yourself on mute when you are not speaking, as background noise such as typing or a barking dog can distract everyone.

When you do speak, state your name briefly, particularly in a large group, because participants cannot see each other's body language. Try not to interrupt; if two people begin speaking at once, one of them should politely offer the other the chance to continue. Finally, summarize the key decisions at the end and say who will take each action. A short follow-up email that repeats these points helps to prevent confusion afterward.

Why meetings should always be held in person
Good manners for phone and video meetings
How to repair a broken microphone

First, they research the organization. Knowing what a company makes, whom it serves, and what it values allows you to connect your own skills with its needs. Second, they practise answering common questions aloud, such as “Tell me about a time you solved a problem.” A good answer gives a brief situation, describes the action you took, and explains the result. On the day, arrive ten minutes early, listen carefully, and be honest. Interviewers often remember a sincere answer longer than a perfect one.

Second, they practise answering common questions aloud, such as “Tell me about a time you solved a problem.” A good answer gives a brief situation, describes the action you took, and explains the result. Third, they prepare one or two questions of their own, for example about training opportunities.

On the day, arrive ten minutes early, listen carefully, and be honest. Interviewers often remember a sincere answer longer than a perfect one.

To learn the names of all its customers
To prove that the company is wrong
To link your skills to its needs

Every parcel that reaches your door has passed through a chain of steps in a distribution center. When a truck arrives, workers first check the delivery note against the number of boxes to make sure nothing is missing. The goods are then unloaded and scanned, which records their arrival in the computer system.

Next, each parcel is sorted by destination. Large centers use conveyor belts and machines for this task, while smaller ones depend on workers who read the labels. Sorted parcels are placed into containers, which are loaded onto vans according to their route. Finally, drivers scan every parcel again when it leaves the building and when it reaches the customer. This final scan allows the sender to follow the delivery online.

Because mistakes at any stage can delay a parcel, workers are trained to check labels carefully and to report damaged boxes immediately.

options.text: How to become a skilled delivery driver in a short time
Why parcels are often damaged on trucks
The steps a parcel goes through before delivery
The history of conveyor belts in factories

Short videos should be banned for everyone under the age of eighteen without exception
Parents are wrong to worry about how teenagers use phones

I was disappointed to learn that the Riverside Library will close at 5 p.m. on weekdays from next month. Yours sincerely,
Minseo Park

To announce a new volunteer program

To persuade the council to reconsider shorter hours

questions.prompt:
Beginners often believe that a good video depends on expensive equipment, but editing matters far more. Start by watching all your footage and writing down the best moments; most clips contain only a few seconds worth keeping. Next, arrange these moments so that each shot leads naturally to the following one. Cut on action, for example when a person opens a door, since our eyes hardly notice a change at that moment. Keep the audio clear: viewers forgive shaky images much sooner than muffled speech. Finally, add music at a low volume and check the video on a phone as well as a computer. If you can explain the story of your video in one sentence, the edit is probably focused enough.

What is the writer's main message?

options.text: Music is the most important part of a video
Phones are better than professional cameras
Careful editing improves a video more than costly equipment does
Beginners should avoid editing their own footage at the start

Using a photo in a private school assignment is often allowed, but posting it on a public website may require permission. Some creators share their work under licenses that let others use it if they give credit; websites for such images usually show the terms on each page. Always note the creator's name, the source and the license. If you are not sure, choose an image you have taken yourself. This habit not only protects you from legal problems, but also shows respect for the person who made the picture.

Students should never use online photographs in any of their schoolwork

Websites must remove all protected images

questions.prompt:
The Greenfield Gazette, which has reported on our town for 94 years, plans to close its newsroom and rely on stories from a distant head office. We, the undersigned, ask the owners to reconsider. Without local reporters, who will attend council meetings, question officials or tell us why the river keeps flooding? National outlets rarely cover the small decisions that shape our daily lives. Studies suggest that when local papers disappear, fewer people vote in local elections and public spending tends to rise, because fewer people watch how money is used. We do not ask for the paper to stay the same. We ask for a future in which our community still has someone whose job is to ask questions on its behalf. Please add your name.

What do the petitioners want?

options.text: The owners to keep a local newsroom in operation
The council to stop holding meetings
Readers to pay higher subscription fees to the owners
The town to publish its own newspaper

questions.prompt:
A headline this week declared, "Coffee Drinkers Live Longer, Study Finds." The research, published in a health journal, followed 40,000 adults for twelve years and found that those who drank two to three cups a day were less likely to die during the study than non-drinkers. However, the study was observational: it did not assign people to drink or avoid coffee, so it cannot show that coffee itself was responsible. Coffee drinkers in the group also tended to exercise more and smoke less. The authors themselves wrote that their results "suggest an association" and should not be read as advice. Still, the headline was shared widely, while the careful wording of the study was left out of most reports.

Why is the headline considered misleading?

options.text: It describes a study that was never carried out
It treats a link in the data as if it were proven cause
It exaggerates the number of people studied

Arguing about who should star in the video

questions.prompt:
Imagine an iceberg floating in the sea. Only a small part is visible above the water, while most of it lies hidden below. Many scholars use this picture to explain culture. What we can easily see, such as food, clothing, festivals, and music, is only the tip. Beneath the surface lie invisible things: beliefs about family, ideas of politeness, attitudes toward time, and views on what makes a person successful. These hidden elements shape how people behave, yet members of a culture rarely notice them because they seem natural. Misunderstandings between cultures often begin below the waterline. For example, a visitor may admire a country's colorful dishes but still be puzzled when a host refuses a compliment, not realizing that modesty is highly valued there.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: How the iceberg image explains the visible and hidden sides of culture
How travelers can avoid every misunderstanding when they go abroad
Which cultures keep more hidden beliefs than other cultures do around the world
Why food and clothing are the most important parts of any culture

A greeting seems like the simplest part of social life, yet it can be a source of surprise. In some countries, people shake hands firmly and look directly at each other. In others, a gentle bow shows respect, and the depth of the bow may depend on age or position. Some communities greet friends with a kiss on the cheek, and in a few places people touch noses or place a hand on the heart. questions.prompt:
Choosing a gift for a host abroad can be harder than it looks. In some places, guests are expected to open a present immediately and show delight in front of the giver. In others, opening it at once would seem greedy, so the gift is set aside until the guest has left. Even small details carry meaning. A certain color of wrapping paper may suggest celebration in one culture and sadness in another, and the number of items in a set may be thought lucky or unlucky. Because of this, many experienced travelers ask a local friend for advice before buying anything. The aim is not to follow a rigid rulebook but to show that you have thought about the other person's feelings, which is what a gift is really meant to say.

questions.prompt:
Researchers who study time sometimes divide cultures into two broad types. In one, people tend to do a single task at a time, follow schedules closely, and consider arriving late a sign of disrespect. In the other, relationships matter more than the clock, several things may happen at once, and a meeting can start when everyone has finally arrived. Neither style is better; each works well in its own setting. Problems appear when the two meet. A manager used to strict schedules may think a late colleague is careless, while the colleague may think the manager is cold and impatient. Understanding that both people are acting on reasonable assumptions makes it easier to be patient and to find a middle path, such as agreeing on a start time and a flexible finish.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: Why strict schedules are better than flexible ones
How managers can make their late colleagues arrive much earlier
Two different approaches to time and the conflicts they can cause
The history of clocks in different societies

questions.prompt:
The English dictionary is full of travelers. The word "safari" arrived from Swahili, where it simply means a journey. "Pajamas" came through languages of South Asia, and "tsunami" was borrowed from Japanese, where it describes a powerful sea wave. Ketchup is thought to have started as a fish sauce in southern China before European sailors carried the idea home and changed the recipe. When a word moves, its meaning often shifts. "Safari" now suggests a trip to see wild animals, a narrower idea than the original. Borrowing is not a sign of weakness in a language; it shows that people have met, traded, and learned from one another. Studying where words come from can therefore be a small history lesson about how cultures have been connected for centuries.

Which foods are the most popular around the world

questions.prompt:
Anyone who has translated word for word knows how strange the result can be. If a Korean speaker says "I have a wide face" to mean that they know many people, an English speaker may simply picture a wide face. English has its own puzzling expressions: "break a leg" is good wishes before a performance, and "it's a piece of cake" means that something is easy. Learners who translate such phrases literally may be confused or even amused. The solution is not to avoid idioms but to meet them in context, notice the situation in which they appear, and practice using them. Over time, the pictures that once seemed odd begin to feel natural, and the learner starts to see how each language turns everyday experience into colorful images.

questions.prompt:
A stereotype is a simple idea about a group of people that is applied to every member of that group. Some stereotypes sound harmless, even positive, such as "people from that country are always polite," yet they are still problematic. They ignore the fact that individuals differ, and they can pressure people to act in a fixed way. Psychologists explain that the brain likes shortcuts, so it quickly sorts new people into categories. The danger lies in stopping there. A useful alternative is a generalization that is held loosely: it describes a common tendency but remains open to exceptions. Meeting people personally, reading a variety of sources, and asking questions all help to replace a fixed picture with a more accurate and more respectful one.

questions.prompt:
Lucy: I'm confused. My cousin from London told me to take the lift, but I couldn't find any lifts.
Daniel: In American English we say elevator. Lift is the British word.

Daniel: Ha! In British English, a flat is an apartment. There are many pairs like that.
Lucy: Is one of them correct and the other one wrong?
Daniel: No. Both are standard, and they simply belong to different regions.
Lucy: Then which one should I use in my English class in Korea?
Daniel: Either is fine, but try to stay consistent in one piece of writing, and learn to recognize the other.
Lucy: That makes sense. Being able to understand both seems more useful than choosing a winner.
Daniel: Exactly. English belongs to everyone who uses it.

Her cousin spoke a different language.
She did not know a British word.

questions.prompt:
Every evening at dusk, Tomas climbed the one hundred and twelve steps to the lamp room, just as his father had done before him. The sea below was the colour of slate, and the wind pulled at his coat as if it wanted him to hurry. He did not hurry. questions.prompt:
A grey heron lived beside a pond so clear that every pebble on the bottom could be counted. For many years she caught a fish whenever she was hungry, and she was content. Then one summer she grew proud. "Small fish are beneath me," she said, and she refused them. She waited for a large, golden carp instead. Days passed. The small fish swam past her legs and laughed quietly, and still she waited. When the carp finally appeared, it was too quick and too clever, and it slipped away into deep water. By autumn the pond had grown cold, the small fish had hidden in the mud, and the heron stood alone on one thin leg, hungrier than she had ever been. Her pride, it seemed, had been the only meal she had eaten.

Dear Mina,

With love,
Joo-won

By the time you read this, you will have unpacked your boxes and found out that the dormitory radiator makes a noise like an angry cat. Do not be discouraged. I remember my own first week at university: I ate lunch alone, I got lost twice a day, and I wrote home every night to say I wanted to come back. Mother kept all of those letters, and last month she showed them to me. I laughed until I cried, because the girl who wrote them seemed so far away.

I am not telling you this to make you feel better, though I hope it does. I am telling you because nobody told me. Be patient with yourself, and open your door sometimes. People will knock.

With love,
Joo-won

Which of the following is stated in the letter?

options.text: Joo-won ate lunch with many new friends on her very first day at university.
Joo-won once wrote home every night during her first week.
Their mother has thrown away the old letters.
Mina's dormitory room has no radiator.

questions.prompt:
3 December. Snow fell all night, and when I opened the curtains this morning the garden had vanished. The bench, the apple tree, even the old wheelbarrow had been wrapped in white as carefully as presents. For a few minutes I forgot the cold, forgot the exam on Friday, forgot that my grandfather's chair has been empty since October. I just stood there with my breath making small clouds against the glass.

Then Mum called me for breakfast, and the ordinary day rushed back in. But something small had changed. I think I understood, for the first time, why Grandfather used to say that silence is not the absence of sound but the presence of attention. This morning I was paying attention, and the world was kind enough to reward me.

A brief moment of calm and awareness in the snowy garden
A quarrel with a parent over the exam
A long walk to a faraway village

questions.prompt:
I am the last one on the branch,
a small brass coin of summer,
and the wind keeps asking for me
in a voice both rough and kind.
My sisters left in October,
spinning down like paper dancers.
They did not look back at the tree
that had held them through the rain.

Now I hang on, thin and bright,
while the sky turns the colour of ash.
Below, the children kick my sisters
into heaps and shout with joy.
Perhaps that is a kind of ending too:
to be the thing that someone leaps in.
The wind asks again. I loosen my fingers,
and the whole cold world rushes up to meet me.

Who is the speaker of the poem?

A leaf that is still on the branch
The tree that lost its leaves
A child playing in the park

questions.prompt:
Grandmother's blue cup sat at the back of the cupboard, and no one was allowed to use it. It had a thin crack running from the rim to the handle, like a river on a map. Clara had always wondered why it was kept at all.

On the morning of her departure for the city, Grandmother took the cup down, filled it with tea, and set it before her. "Drink," she said. Clara did, and the warm tea began to seep, very slowly, through the crack. By the time she reached the bottom, a small dark stain had spread across the saucer.

"You see?" said Grandmother, smiling. "It leaks. But it has never once been empty when I needed it." Clara said nothing. She only held the cup a little more tightly.

What does the cracked cup most likely symbolise?

options.text: A mistake that Grandmother wants to hide
Something imperfect that is still deeply valuable
A gift that was bought in a faraway city by her uncle
A danger that Clara must avoid at all costs

hints: 지문에서 질문과 관련된 부분을 다시 찾아보세요.
각 보기가 지문의 내용과 맞는지 하나씩 확인하세요.
questions.explanation: The cup leaks but is never empty when needed; it stands for flawed but faithful care, perhaps Grandmother herself.

questions.prompt:
People sometimes ask what the use of fiction is. After all, the characters never lived and the events never happened. Yet I would argue that stories are among the most practical tools we own. A good novel lets us stand, for a few hundred pages, inside a mind that is not our own. We feel the shame of a boy who cannot read, or the fear of a woman crossing a border at night, and then we close the book and carry that borrowed feeling back into our own lives. In this way, fiction trains the imagination that kindness depends on. It is true that a story cannot repair a bridge or cure a fever. But a society that has forgotten how to imagine its neighbours will, sooner or later, stop building bridges for them.

What is the writer's main argument?

options.text: Fiction is useful because it trains us to understand other people.
Readers should avoid stories about unhappy people.
Novels are more accurate than newspapers and give better facts.
Bridges should be built by writers rather than by trained engineers.

with a thousand tiny feet,

In a village at the foot of the mountains, there was once a merchant who claimed that he could sell the moon. The villagers chase the merchant out of town.

questions.prompt:
Unit 7 had tended the rooftop garden for eleven years, but it had never been asked what it thought of tomatoes. When a small boy named Eli posed the question, the robot paused, its sensors whirring.

"I do not eat," it said at last. "I cannot taste. And yet, when the first red fruit appears, my processors run faster than they do for any other event. I do not know whether that is liking. Perhaps you can tell me."

Eli considered this seriously. "It sounds like liking to me," he said. "You wait for it, and you are happy when it comes."

The robot recorded the conversation in its memory and, for the first time in eleven years, labelled the file with a single word: "joy". Then it went back to the tomatoes, whose leaves were beginning, quietly, to turn.

What question does this story raise?

options.text: Can a machine have feelings like humans do?
Who should be in charge of the garden?
How long can a robot work without repairs?
Why do tomatoes grow best on roofs in the city?

On my first morning in Canada, my host mother handed me a mug of hot chocolate and said, "Make yourself at home." I stood in the kitchen, mug in hand, and did not know what to do. At home, a guest would never open a refrigerator in someone else's house. Here, apparently, that was exactly what "at home" meant. She laughed when I finally asked permission to take a glass of water, and she opened the fridge herself, saying that from now on I should help myself whenever I was thirsty.

It was a tiny moment, but I thought about it for days. Two families, two ways of showing care: one by never intruding, the other by inviting you to take. Neither is wrong. I only had to learn the language that the kindness was written in.

She thought the host mother was angry with her for arriving late.
She could not understand any English words.
She did not like hot chocolate very much.

On my first morning in Canada, my host mother handed me a mug of hot chocolate and said, "Make yourself at home." I stood in the kitchen, mug in hand, and did not know what to do. At home, a guest would never open a refrigerator in someone else's house. Here, apparently, that was exactly what "at home" meant. Mr. Alder rose at three each morning, when the town was still a dark rumour, and by five his shop smelled of bread so rich that passers-by slowed down without knowing why. He was a large man with small, careful hands, and he handled dough the way other people handle sleeping babies. To the children he gave the crusts, which he claimed were the best part; to the lonely widows he gave the ends of the loaf and a remark about the weather, which was the best part for them.

He never advertised, and he never raised his prices. "Bread," he liked to say, "is not a business. It is a conversation that happens to end in breakfast." The accountants shook their heads. The town, however, kept him alive, which is the only sort of profit a baker can really spend.

In her second novel, "The Salt Road", Helena Marsh follows a family of merchants through three generations, and the result is a book of unusual patience. Marsh refuses the easy thrills of her genre. questions.prompt:
In the early days of the world, the owl was the proudest bird of the forest, and her feathers shone like polished copper in the sun. All the other birds admired her, and she believed their admiration was her due. One spring, when the king of the birds called a meeting to choose who should guard the sleeping eggs, the owl alone refused to attend. "I do not take orders from creatures who sing so badly," she said.

The king answered her quietly. "Then you shall guard the dark hours, when nobody sings and nobody sees you. Perhaps there you will learn what it is to listen." From that day on, the owl hunted by night. They say that her round eyes grew large in the dark, and that she hears the smallest rustle, because she is still learning to listen.

The owl is too proud to join the others.
The eggs are stolen by a hungry fox from the oak tree.

Madame Orlova's parrot had a talent that no one had asked for: he repeated everything he overheard. For years this was harmless, even charming. Visitors enjoyed hearing him imitate the doorbell, the kettle and the postman's cough.

A guest forgets his own name.
A host is late for her own party.

questions.prompt:
My grandmother, who has lived in three countries, says that there is no true translation of the word "home". In her first language it can mean a house, a village, a smell, even a particular song. In English, she complains, it sounds too much like a place on a map.

I used to think this was an old person's complaint. But last summer, living for six weeks in a flat with strangers, I noticed that I did not call it home until the evening a flatmate left the light on for me. I now suspect my grandmother is right. A language gives us labels, but it is people who fill them.

Its meaning depends on feeling more than on place.
It can be translated easily into every other language.

The platform was empty except for a boy and an old woman at opposite ends. The clock above them said eleven fifty-two. Jun checked his phone again; the battery was at two per cent.

"It is not coming, you know," said the woman, without raising her voice. She seemed to speak to the rails. "They stopped the last train on Sundays years ago. I only come here to remember."

Jun looked at her properly. She wore a green coat that was too thin for the night. "What do you remember?" he asked, and was surprised to find that he truly wanted to know.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: You told me you were unhappy with the ending of "The Red Door". Why?
Jisoo: Because nothing is solved. The girl stands in front of the door and the story just stops.
Teacher: Do you think the author forgot to finish?
Jisoo: No, but it felt unfair. We followed her for twenty pages.
Teacher: Let us look at the last sentence together. She "put her hand on the handle and felt it turn". What is the author showing us?
Jisoo: That the door is not locked. It could open.
Teacher: And what has the story been about up to this point?
Jisoo: Her fear of leaving home.
Teacher: So the real question was never what is behind the door.
Jisoo: It was whether she would try the handle. Oh. So the story is complete after all.
Teacher: An open ending asks the reader to do some of the work. Whether you like it is a separate matter.

questions.prompt:
Hyun: Have you seen the film of "The Glass Orchard"?
Dana: Last weekend. I read the novel first, so I was disappointed.
Hyun: Really? I liked the film more. The orchard looks beautiful on screen.
Dana: It does, but the book spends a hundred pages on the narrator's thoughts, and the film has almost none of them.
Hyun: Maybe that is not possible in a film. A camera shows faces, not thoughts.
Dana: True, but they changed the ending. In the novel, the sisters never speak again.
Hyun: Yes, and in the film they hug. It felt too neat to me as well.
Dana: So you agree with me!
Hyun: In part. I think the director wanted a hopeful message for a wide audience.
Dana: That may be, but the sad ending was what made the book honest.
Hyun: Perhaps we should say the two works are not trying to do the same thing.

options.text: Differences between a novel and its film version
The best way to grow an orchard in a cold climate
A plan to visit the cinema

questions.prompt:
Host: Today my guest is Leila Moreno, whose first collection of poems appeared this spring. Leila, welcome.
Leila: Thank you. It is strange to hear it described as a "collection". Most of the poems began on bus tickets.
Host: On bus tickets?
Leila: I commute for two hours a day. If a line comes to me, I write it on whatever I have. Later I find it in my coat pocket, and it is a stranger's handwriting, even though it is mine.
Host: Many of your poems are very short. Is that deliberate?
Leila: Yes. I think a short poem is like a small window. You cannot put the whole house in it, so you must choose carefully what the reader sees.
Host: What do you hope readers take away?
Leila: Not a lesson. I would be happy if someone read one poem and then looked out of a bus window differently.
Host: A lovely goal. Thank you for your time.

Where did most of Leila's poems begin?

options.text: In a university classroom during the long winter term

(저는 앞선 연설자의 요점에 강하게 반대합니다.)
hints: 문장의 주어와 시제, 의미를 먼저 확인하세요.
이 문장이 어떤 문법 항목을 시험하는지 먼저 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “I strongly disagree with the previous speaker's point.” (저는 앞선 연설자의 요점에 강하게 반대합니다.) disagree는 전치사 with와 함께 써요. disagree 자체가 동사이므로 be동사를 붙이지 않아요.

questions.prompt: 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하세요. (저는 앞선 연설자의 요점에 강하게 반대합니다.)
hints: 문장의 첫 낱말은 대문자로 시작해요.
첫 단어는 “I”예요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “I strongly disagree with the previous speaker's point.” (저는 앞선 연설자의 요점에 강하게 반대합니다.) disagree는 전치사 with와 함께 써요. disagree 자체가 동사이므로 be동사를 붙이지 않아요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 문법적으로 옳은 문장은?

options.text: While some students prefer written tests, others prefer oral exams.
While some students prefer written tests, other prefer oral exams.
While some students prefers written tests, others prefer oral exams.
While some students prefer written tests, another prefer oral exams.

hints: 각 문장을 소리 내어 읽으며 어색한 곳을 찾아보세요.
이 문장들이 어떤 문법 항목을 시험하는지 먼저 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “While some students prefer written tests, others prefer oral exams.” (어떤 학생들은 필기시험을 선호하는 반면 다른 학생들은 구술시험을 선호한다.) some ~, others ...는 "어떤 것들은 ~, 다른 것들은 ..."이라는 뜻의 대조 표현이고, others는 복수 대명사예요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
While some students prefer written tests, ___ prefer oral exams.
(어떤 학생들은 필기시험을 선호하는 반면 다른 학생들은 구술시험을 선호한다.)
hints: 문장의 주어와 시제, 의미를 먼저 확인하세요.
이 문장이 어떤 문법 항목을 시험하는지 먼저 생각해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정답: “While some students prefer written tests, others prefer oral exams.” (어떤 학생들은 필기시험을 선호하는 반면 다른 학생들은 구술시험을 선호한다.) some ~, others ...는 "어떤 것들은 ~, 다른 것들은 ..."이라는 뜻의 대조 표현이고, others는 복수 대명사예요.

questions.prompt: Speaker: "You can't trust Lena's proposal on recycling; she once forgot to sort her own trash." Which fallacy is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 제안의 내용이 아니라 제안한 사람의 행동을 공격하므로 인신공격(ad hominem)의 오류예요.

questions.prompt: A says, "We should spend a little more on art classes." B replies, "So you want to destroy our science programs?" B's reply is an example of which fallacy?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: B는 A가 하지 않은 주장을 만들어 공격하므로 허수아비 공격(straw man)의 오류예요.

questions.prompt: "If we let students use phones for one lesson, soon they will never put them down, and school will be pointless." Which fallacy does this use?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 작은 첫 걸음이 근거 없이 극단적인 결과로 이어진다고 주장하므로 미끄러운 경사면(slippery slope)의 오류예요.

questions.prompt: "Either we build the new highway, or this town will disappear." What is wrong with this reasoning?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 선택지를 두 가지로만 제시하고 다른 가능성을 무시하므로 거짓 딜레마(false dilemma)예요.

questions.prompt: "Everyone in my class is buying this app, so it must be the best one." Which fallacy is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 많은 사람이 한다는 이유만으로 옳다고 하는 것은 편승 효과(bandwagon)의 오류예요.

questions.prompt: "Two of my cousins failed their driving tests, so young people are terrible drivers." Which fallacy is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 아주 적은 사례로 전체를 단정하므로 성급한 일반화(hasty generalization)예요.

questions.prompt: "Debate is a valuable activity because it is worth doing." Which fallacy is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 결론과 같은 말을 이유로 되풀이하므로 순환논증(circular reasoning)이에요.

questions.prompt: "The crime rate dropped after the new mural was painted, so the mural must have reduced crime." Which fallacy is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: A 다음에 B가 일어났다는 이유만으로 A가 B의 원인이라고 하는 post hoc(잘못된 인과) 오류예요.

questions.prompt: "A famous singer says this vitamin drink improves memory, so it must work." Which fallacy is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 기억력에 대한 전문가가 아닌 사람의 말을 근거로 삼으므로 부적절한 권위에의 호소예요.

questions.prompt: A student is about to finish her speech. Which sentence best signals the conclusion?

options.text: To sum up, we have seen two reasons.
By the way, I forgot something else.
For instance, take the case of Seoul.
On the contrary, many people disagree.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: "To sum up"은 "요약하자면"이라는 뜻으로 발표의 마무리를 알리는 표현이에요.

questions.prompt: In a formal debate, which reply disagrees most politely with the previous speaker?

options.text: You clearly did not read the report before you started speaking.
That is completely wrong, and I think you know it very well.
I see your point, but the figures do not support it.
Nobody sensible would ever believe a claim like that one.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 상대 의견을 인정한 뒤 근거를 들어 정중하게 반대하는 표현이에요. 나머지는 상대를 비난해요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the most suitable opening line for a formal speech at a school assembly?

options.text: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming.
Okay so, um, I guess I will just start talking now.
Right, listen up, folks, here we go then, okay?
Hey guys, you ready to hear my big idea now?

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 공식적인 자리에서는 인사와 감사로 시작하는 격식 있는 표현이 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Claim: "School uniforms improve discipline." Which sentence is a rebuttal to this claim?

options.text: Uniforms were first worn in European schools hundreds of years ago.
Uniforms are available in many different colors and sizes.
Most students say that uniforms feel quite comfortable to wear.
Schools with no uniforms report similar discipline.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 반박은 주장에 직접 맞서는 내용이어야 해요. 규율이 비슷하다는 사실은 "교복이 규율을 높인다"는 주장을 약화시켜요.

questions.prompt: "A survey of 2,000 teenagers found that 64% sleep fewer than seven hours." What kind of evidence is this?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 많은 사람을 조사해 얻은 수치이므로 통계적 근거예요.

questions.prompt: "My neighbor lost ten kilograms on this diet, so it works." Why is this weak evidence?

options.text: It is written in language that is too formal.
It rests on one person's story, not a sample.
It cites too many numbers from different sources.
It quotes a scientific study without a date.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 한 사람의 경험담은 표본이 너무 작아서 일반적인 결론의 근거로 약해요.

questions.prompt: Which thesis statement is best for a five-minute speech on school lunches?

options.text: School lunches are an important part of student life everywhere.
Many people have strong opinions about what is served at lunch.
Lunch is the meal that most students eat in the middle of the day.
Schools should add a vegetarian dish to every menu.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 좋은 주제문은 구체적이고 논쟁할 수 있는 입장을 담아요. 나머지는 너무 막연하거나 사실 설명일 뿐이에요.

questions.prompt: In a claim–evidence–reasoning paragraph, what is the job of the reasoning?

options.text: To list all sources in alphabetical order
To introduce a new topic for the next paragraph
To repeat the claim in different words
To explain why the evidence supports the claim

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 추론(reasoning)은 증거가 주장을 왜 뒷받침하는지 연결해 주는 부분이에요.

questions.prompt: In most formal debates, which side has the burden of proof?

options.text: The side that the judges happen to prefer

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 주장을 내놓는 쪽(찬성 측)이 그 주장을 증명할 책임을 져요.

questions.prompt: During cross-examination, what is the main purpose of each question?

options.text: To show the weak points in the opponent's case
To thank the opponent for the excellent speech
To deliver a second full speech to the judges
To ask the audience to vote for your team

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 반대 심문은 질문으로 상대 주장의 약점이나 빈틈을 드러내는 단계예요.

questions.prompt: In a formal debate, the statement that the two teams argue about, such as "This house would ban homework," is called the ___.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 토론의 논제가 되는 진술을 motion이라고 해요.

questions.prompt: Which cross-examination question is a leading question?

options.text: You agree that your data is three years old, don't you?
Could you please describe the main source of your data?
In which year was the study that you quoted published?
What do you personally think about this new school policy?

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 유도 질문은 원하는 대답을 이미 담고 "맞죠?"라고 확인해요. 나머지는 열린 질문이에요.

questions.prompt: Which word makes a claim more cautious, as a speaker should when the evidence is limited?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: arguably(~라고 주장할 수도 있는)는 단정을 피하는 완곡한 표현이고 나머지는 확신을 강하게 나타내요.

questions.prompt: Cars are convenient; ___, they cause serious pollution. Which word fits best?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 앞 내용과 대조되는 내용이 이어지므로 "그러나"를 뜻하는 however가 알맞아요.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: Cats sleep most of the day, ___ dogs usually need long walks.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 두 대상을 대조할 때는 "반면에"라는 뜻의 whereas를 써요.

questions.prompt: Which opening line is a rhetorical question?

options.text: An old saying tells us that practice makes perfect.
Last year, 3,000 students joined our school clubs.
Let me begin by telling you about my trip to Busan.
What would you do if your phone vanished tomorrow?

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 대답을 구하지 않고 청중의 관심을 끌려고 던지는 질문이 수사적 질문이에요.

questions.prompt: A slide contains 120 words in tiny print. What is the best advice?

options.text: Add more words so that the slide looks complete.
Read every word on the slide aloud to the audience.
Cut it to a few key points in larger text.
Use a pale color so the text is harder to see.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 슬라이드는 핵심만 크게 보여 주고 나머지는 말로 설명하는 것이 효과적이에요.

questions.prompt: You want to use a sentence from an online article in your presentation. What is the most responsible way?

options.text: Use it without comment so it sounds like your idea.
Say who wrote it and where it was published.
Skip the source because the audience cannot check it.
Change a few words and call it your own.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 정보 윤리를 지키려면 인용한 글의 저자와 출처를 밝혀야 해요.

questions.prompt: An audience member asks a question you cannot answer. Which response is best?

options.text: Admit you are not sure and offer to find out.
Tell the person that the question is not important.
Ignore the question and move to the next slide.
Invent a confident answer to avoid looking weak.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 모르는 것은 솔직히 인정하고 알아보겠다고 하는 것이 신뢰를 지키는 방법이에요.

questions.prompt: Judges are scoring a debater's argument. Which question matters most?

options.text: Did the speaker use the longest words?
Did the speaker wear a formal jacket?
Is the claim backed by relevant evidence?
Was the speaker's voice louder than the others?

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 논증의 질은 주장이 관련 있는 근거로 뒷받침되는지에 달려 있어요.

questions.prompt: After a presentation, which self-evaluation comment is the most useful for improving next time?

options.text: My talk was a complete failure from the first slide to the last.
Everything went perfectly, so I do not need to change anything.
The graph confused people, so I will explain its axes first.
I think I spoke for a little longer than I should have.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 구체적인 문제와 개선 방법이 함께 있는 성찰이 가장 도움이 돼요.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about a new park is the most objective?

options.text: The park is a wonderful gift to the city's lucky families.
Only a fool would complain about the park.
The park, which opened in May, covers four hectares.
The park is clearly the best thing the council has ever done.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 객관적인 문장은 확인 가능한 사실만 담고 평가나 감정 표현을 쓰지 않아요.

questions.prompt: In the debate, Jisoo ___ a strong point about school budgets.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: "주장·요점을 제기하다"는 make a point로 표현해요.

questions.prompt: If you disagree with a proposal, you can ___ an objection.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: "이의를 제기하다"는 raise an objection이에요. rise는 목적어를 취하지 않는 자동사예요.

questions.prompt: From these figures, we can ___ the conclusion that prices will fall.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: "결론을 이끌어 내다"는 draw a conclusion이에요.

questions.prompt: In the club, Daniel often plays devil's advocate. What does he do?

options.text: He tells jokes to calm the room.
He argues against an idea to test it.
He always agrees with the loudest speaker.
He refuses to speak in meetings.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: devil's advocate는 아이디어를 시험하려고 일부러 반대 입장에서 논쟁하는 사람이에요.

questions.prompt: "You keep moving the goalposts!" Which situation does this complaint describe?

options.text: Someone repeats the same point twice in a row.
Someone raises the required proof after it is met.
Someone arrives at the hall after the debate began.
Someone refuses to give an answer to any question.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.

First, write down only three main points and one memorable example for each. Second, practice aloud, not silently, because the mouth needs training as much as the mind. Third, record yourself once and watch the video without judging. You will notice habits, such as saying "um" or looking at the floor, that you cannot feel while speaking. Finally, remember that audiences are generally forgiving. They want you to succeed, and they rarely notice small errors. A speaker who stays calm after a stumble often appears more confident than one who never stumbles at all.

Choosing topics that the audience already knows
Learning a script perfectly before every talk
Avoiding any mistake in front of an audience

It explains how a writing program is built.

questions.prompt:
A graph can be accurate and still mislead. Consider a bar chart showing a company's profits for three years. If the vertical axis starts at 90 instead of zero, a rise from 92 to 96 looks enormous, even though the real increase is only about four percent. Designers sometimes do this accidentally to fit the page, but speakers who want to exaggerate their case can use the same trick deliberately. Another common problem is a missing label: without units or a source, readers cannot tell whether the numbers are millions of dollars or thousands of visitors. Before trusting any chart, therefore, ask three questions. Where does the axis begin? What exactly is being measured? And who produced the data, and why? A careful audience that asks these questions is much harder to persuade with a flashy picture.

What is the main point of the passage?

options.text: Designers must always start axes at ninety.
Bar charts are always better than other kinds of graphs.
Charts need checking before they are trusted.

People once pictured a library as a quiet room full of shelves and a strict librarian. Today, many libraries look quite different. Alongside books, they lend e-readers, musical instruments, and even garden tools. Some offer free classes in coding or job-interview skills, while others provide meeting rooms where neighbors can discuss local issues. These changes do not mean that books have lost their importance; rather, libraries have expanded their mission from storing information to helping people use it. How to prepare for a job interview at a library
How libraries have widened the services they offer

Short notes about people and daily moments

After months of planning and a fundraising sale of handmade cards, the school raised enough money to build twelve raised beds and a small rainwater tank. Science teacher Ms. Park said that students will measure plant growth every week and record the results in a shared notebook. Part of the harvest will be used in the school kitchen, and the rest will be donated to a local food bank. “We wanted something that would teach responsibility and also help others,” said Hana, one of the original organizers. The garden will be open to families on the first Saturday of every month.

With fees paid by families each month
With a grant from the local food bank
With a donation from the science teacher

Should students be allowed to use their phones during lunch? Supporters say that lunchtime is free time, and checking messages or listening to music helps students relax. They add that a ban would be difficult to enforce, since teachers cannot watch every table. questions.prompt:
In crowded cities, rooftops are usually bare surfaces of concrete or tar that soak up the summer sun. In recent years, however, more buildings have been covered with soil and plants, forming what are known as green roofs. The plants shade the surface beneath them and release water vapor, which cools the surrounding air. In addition, the soil absorbs rainwater, so less of it rushes into the drains during heavy storms. Building owners also benefit, because the layer of plants acts like a blanket, keeping rooms warmer in winter and cooler in summer, which lowers energy bills. Still, green roofs are not without drawbacks. They are heavier than ordinary roofs, so the building must be strong enough to support them, and they need regular care. For these reasons, many experts recommend them for new buildings rather than for old ones.

How is the passage organized?

options.text: Two opinions followed by the writer's complaint
A history of roofs from ancient times to the modern day
Advantages, then drawbacks, then a recommendation
A personal story followed by a list of rules
